title: Would more rows help? A learning curve on the training folds, with a plain answer (34.13)
request: The owner's map of DCLab's abilities names data as a weak layer: nothing says whether more rows or which labels would help. The plan (docs/guides/PHASE10_ABILITIES_PLAN.md, 34.13) asks for an honest, measured answer a person can act on.
spec: A learning curve on the training folds only (25, 50, 75 and 100 % of each fold's fit rows; whole groups when grouped, the latest rows when timed, within each class otherwise), the score at each size with an interval, the last step's gain with its 90 % interval, an answer (likely_help, unlikely_help, cannot_tell) with its assumption, and the same per segment; never the holdout; captured as a ledger point and an event.
plan: read the existing learning-curve contract and decide whether to extend it
a core function taking the host's trainer, fitted inside each fold
replicas with a known curve, rising and flat
a studio analysis, its route and job, apart from the stage records
capture: ledger point data.more_rows and a decision.proposed event

decisions.decision: A separate contract (DataValue) from the store's LearningCurve
decisions.why: LearningCurve is knowledge across builds and never names anything of a table; this is one project's measurement and names the segments of the customer's own table

decisions.decision: The answer reads the last step's gain and its interval: likely help only when the interval is above zero
decisions.why: a noisy flat curve must not say more rows help; measured on pure-noise tables it never did

decisions.decision: A separate analysis and job, never a change to a stage record
decisions.why: the stage records are what every number is traced to; an advice must not change them

change: dclab_core/data_value.py (DataValue v1, SizeScore, learning_curve) and replicas/learning_curves.py; dclab_core ledger point data.more_rows, conformance, contracts, schemas, 0.107.0; dclab_rnd/studio/data_value.py; jobs/handlers.py (data_value); ledger capture more_rows; experience hook data_value_measured; routers/projects.py (POST and GET /api/projects/{id}/data-value) and the web client; agentic/services.py (busy entry); CORE_INTEGRATION.md; the wheel check's smoke; docs/DATA_CATALOG.md regenerated; tests (core 12, studio 7, experience log).

findings.defect: a second request while one was queued crashed instead of saying the project was busy
findings.scenario: posting the measurement twice with wait false: the first queued, the second answered with an internal error
findings.cause: the busy messages had no entry for this kind of job, so looking it up raised
findings.fix: the job's busy message added; a route test posts twice and expects the busy answer
findings.impact: an error page for a double click
alternatives: pass the busy message from the route

findings.defect: the new write route did not say what it records
findings.scenario: the experience log's test lists every write route and what it records; the new route was missing
findings.cause: the route was added without its entry
findings.fix: the route records a decision.proposed event, and says so
findings.impact: a route whose capture nobody checks

findings.defect: the data catalog had not been regenerated for three new contracts
findings.scenario: decision_spec (34.1), prediction_record and outcome_record (34.9) and data_value were missing from docs/DATA_CATALOG.md
findings.cause: the earlier packages ran make core-schemas but not make catalog
findings.fix: make catalog run; the catalog carries all four
findings.impact: the full gate would have failed on the committed packages

findings.defect: the new learning-curves replica entered the business-examples knowledge base with no pitfalls, and the committed base went stale
findings.scenario: test_business_examples on main after 782c7307: replica:learning_curves states no pitfall (its docstring had no traps section and no sentence the builder reads as one), and evidence/business_examples was not rebuilt
findings.cause: every replica's docstring is read by dclab_rnd/business_examples.py as a knowledge-base entry; the package's own tests did not include that file, and the full gate was owed
findings.fix: a traps section in the replica's docstring (the holdout is not a curve's yardstick; subsets keep the split's shape; two points are not a slope; a flat curve is not a finished model; an average hides a segment), and make business-examples

measurements.name: the answer on replicas with a known curve, ten seeds each
measurements.gate: a rising curve says likely help, a flat one unlikely help
measurements.result: rising 9 of 10 likely help and 1 cannot tell; flat 10 of 10 unlikely help

measurements.name: false alarms on pure-noise tables (the review)
measurements.result: 60 runs over three model families and two sizes: 0 likely help, 55 cannot tell, 5 unlikely help

outcome: A project whose models stage ran can ask whether more rows would help: the curve on its training folds, the answer with its interval and assumption, and the segments where errors gather, captured as a decision; the held-back cases are never read.
lessons: A new route needs its capture declared as much as its code.
Regenerate every derived file a contract touches, not only its schema.
A new replica is also a knowledge-base entry: write its traps section and rebuild the business examples in the same commit
risks: segment names stay in the project record only; any new reader must keep them out of the ledger and events
